title: Electric Circuits
summary: How a battery, wires and a bulb make a closed loop, and why a switch works.

steps.title: A loop for electricity
sentences: Electricity needs a complete path to flow, called a circuit.
A simple circuit has a battery or cell, wires and a bulb.
When the loop is closed the bulb lights, and when there is a gap the bulb stays dark.

steps.title: Switches
sentences: A switch opens or closes the loop.
When the switch is off, there is a gap, so the electricity cannot flow.
When it is on, the gap is closed and the bulb glows.

steps.title: Conductors and insulators
sentences: Materials that let electricity pass easily are called conductors, such as copper and iron.
Materials that do not let it pass are called insulators, such as rubber, plastic and wood.
Wires are copper inside for flow and covered with plastic for safety.

steps.title: Staying safe
sentences: Never put anything into a plug socket, and never touch electrical things with wet hands.
Household electricity is very strong and can be dangerous.
Practice with small batteries only, under the eye of an adult.

facts: The electricity in our homes in India is at 230 volts, much stronger than a torch battery of 1.5 volts.
Metals such as copper and silver are very good conductors.
Lightning is a huge natural spark of electricity.

quiz.q: What must a circuit have for a bulb to glow?
quiz.why: The path must be closed all the way round.
Plastic does not let electricity pass.
A switch opens or closes the circuit.
